transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-04-13 09:30 UTC | Duration: ~45m | Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Samir (Redwood SE), Maya (Orion PM), Jules (Infra), Diego (ML), Priya (Security)

[00:00] Alex: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we'll kick off — appreciate you all making time. quick agenda: bench review, model selection, pinning/canary plan, security check. sound good?
[00:10] Maya: yep, sounds good. quick note, we've got Diego on for ML numbers and Jules for infra notes.
[00:18] Samir: hi all. I posted the updated benchmark sheet last night — link in chat — it's the one with the 3 scenarios: low-latency, cost-optimized, and quality heavy.
[00:30] Diego: cool, real quick on the data set we used the 1k queries from our search chat logs, anonymized. small noise but representative.
[00:42] Alex: perfect. so top-level — the open-llm-3b-lite is cheapest but quality hit on longer prompts, the redwood-2-small-ish (note: transcription sometimes shows RedWood 2) sits in middle, and the large gpt-compat models are best quality but 2.5-3x cost.
[01:05] Maya: can you share p95 numbers again? the sheet has p50/p95 and cost per 1k tokens.
[01:12] Samir: yeah, p50 for redwood-2-small ~ 120ms, p95 ~ 420ms on our dev dedicated pool. open-llm-3b-lite p95 ~ 300ms but hallucination rate up for our QA tests. gpt-compat-large p95 ~ 520ms unless we enable batching aggressively.
[01:35] Jules: infra note — when p95 goes above ~400 the UX team sees timeouts in the front end, so we need to either fallback to a smaller model or increase timeout. not ideal.
[01:50] Maya: ok that frames it. Diego, on quality tradeoffs: are hallucinations acceptable in certain routes? we have a small commerce taxonomy where accuracy is critical (price, SKU mapping).
[02:05] Diego: right, for taxonomy we need high precision; for the conversational helper we can tolerate lower precision. so suggestion: pin taxonom route to gpt-compat-large or redwood-2-small with stricter prompting, and the chit-chat route to open-llm-3b-lite.
[02:30] Samir: that's consistent with Redwood runtime routing — you can set route-level pinning and automatic fallback to a cheaper variant on overload. note: the fallback config currently supports model variant and region fallback, and we demoed KV cache to speed up repeated prefixes.
[02:50] Priya: question — what about data residency and KMS? we need confirmation that logs and model input are not leaving our VPC for the private deployment.
[03:03] Alex: for the Private option we have the control plane in your VPC, and you can use your KMS/HSM. Samir, maybe you can remind them about audit logs?
[03:11] Samir: yeah, audit logs are retained in the customer's account for Private; for Dedicated hosted we provide streaming logs to your SIEM via the connector. KMS keys can be customer-provided, we accept ARN.
[03:25] Priya: ok, we'll validate. please include the exact KMS key usage note in the security doc.
[03:32] Alex: will do. back to pinning — today's ask is: decide on pin for taxonomy route and a canary for the general chat route. Maya, where are you leaning?
[03:42] Maya: leaning to pin taxonomy to redwood-2-small v1.4 (we saw better precision) and canary chat to open-llm-3b-lite for 10% traffic. but concerned about p95 spikes.
[03:55] Samir: we can do canary for 72 hours, enable KV cache for that route which reduced p95 by ~25% in our dev run — remember that caching is prefix-based and depends on prompt structure so results vary.
[04:12] Diego: in our tests enabling KV cache cut repeated prompt latency significantly; one caveat: it increases memory on the GPU side. Jules, is memory pressure okay?
[04:22] Jules: depends on host size. On the smaller Dedicated nodes we're at ~75% already when running two shards. we can add burst nodes for canary but it's additional cost.
[04:32] Maya: cost we can absorb for two days. main thing is to see regression on quality.
[04:40] Alex: ok plan proposal: pin taxonomy to redwood-2-small v1.4 (no canary), canary chat route to open-llm-3b-lite v0.9 for 10% traffic, enable KV cache for canary, monitor p95 and hallucination metric; rollback to redwood-2-small if hallucination above threshold or p95 > 400 for 2 consecutive hours.
[05:05] Maya: agreed. question on rollback automation — can we auto-fallback?
[05:10] Samir: yes, runtime supports an automated fallback policy: if latency or error threshold breached, route can swap to a pre-configured fallback model instantly; that's how we avoid timeouts. note there's a small rewarm penalty for KV cache mismatch.
[05:28] Diego: also note that when we switch models there may be slight tokenization differences so downstream scoring can move. we should flag that in the evals.
[05:38] Priya: security-wise, automated rollbacks are fine but we need an audit trail of when they happen.
[05:44] Alex: audit logs capture rollout changes and automated policy triggers with timestamps — we'll include sample logs.
[05:50] Maya: awesome. any competitor concerns? Jules asked about Anthropic's latency numbers.
[05:57] Jules: right we ran a quick bench vs Anthropic and OpenAI — Anthropic had consistent latency but cost was higher; OpenAI was fast but opaque around caching and deduping.
[06:10] Alex: that's consistent with what we see; Redwood gives you visibility into per-token cost and cache hits which helps optimize.
[06:20] Samir: quick demo snippet — I can show the pinning UI and how to set canary percentages, but I'll just talk through it now since we have a full agenda: you pick the route, select model version (e.g., redwood-2-small:v1.4), choose canary percent, set thresholds for p95 and hallucination score, and pick fallback.
[06:40] Maya: does the hallucination score require human annotation?
[06:45] Diego: yes we instrument a small sample of responses to evaluate hallucination rates; can be human or metric-based heuristics. we used a mix.
[06:53] Maya: ok. on the canary duration — you mentioned 72 hours — good enough for us.
[06:58] Samir: yes 72 hours, metrics streamed to the console, and we can push a daily snapshot to your S3.
[07:06] Alex: action item recap coming after call. now quick walk through of the benchmark sheet items we flagged:
[07:15] Samir: (reads) scenario A — taxonomy. redwood-2-small:v1.4 accuracy 96.2% cost 0.8x baseline latency p95 410ms. scenario B — conversation. open-llm-3b-lite:v0.9 cost 0.3x baseline latency p95 300ms but hallucination 6.8%. scenario C — fallback large model gpt-compat-large cost 2.6x baseline, latency p95 520ms.
[07:50] Maya: those numbers align with what we saw. Diego: any outliers?
[07:56] Diego: one outlier for the redwood-2 run — a sequence of long prompts spiked to 780ms partly due to cache miss and longer KV warm.
[08:06] Jules: that suggests for long sessions we either need longer timeouts or different shard sizing.
[08:12] Alex: noted. next up — docs & links. I'll send the benchmark CSV, the recommended rollout yaml for the canary, and security snippets.
[08:22] Maya: please add the exact KMS key usage and how logs are delivered to our SIEM.
[08:28] Priya: also need an SLA note for canary traffic — if canary fails we need a notification flow.
[08:35] Samir: alerting can be hooked to PagerDuty via webhook, we can add runbooks to the console.
[08:41] Maya: great. Diego: small note — please include tokenization differences in the shared doc so model comparisons are apples-to-apples.
[08:49] Alex: will do.
[08:55] Maya: any blockers from Redwood side?
[08:58] Alex: nothing — we can provision the canary pin and enable KV cache in dev in the next two days. Samir: I just need permission to toggle canary in your dev account.
[09:07] Jules: granted for the dev env. we'll restrict prod toggles to a smaller team.
[09:12] Maya: ok. last question — if we want mid-canary rollback, what's the latency on fallback? immediate but with a small rewarm — correct?
[09:21] Samir: immediate switch, rewarm depends on cache, expect a few hundred milliseconds for initial requests.
[09:27] Maya: fine.
[09:30] Alex: recap of next steps: Alex sends assets, Samir provisions canary, Maya runs validation, Priya shares security answers. we'll reconvene in a week or earlier if issues.
[09:40] Maya: thanks everyone.
[09:43] Alex: thanks, bye.

Notes: transcript includes minor transcription artifacts (model names sometimes spelled RedWood or redwood-2-small vs redwood2). References: benchmark spreadsheet (link in chat), rollout yaml (link to console), security questionnaire (link to drive).
